scope: Twenty-second expansion batch: 12 controlled noun/adjective predicate exercises. Six matched pairs contain two nouns (student, vacant lot), two na-adjectives (quiet, clean) and two i-adjectives (cold, expensive). Six retained-state mama answers contrast with six naru changes, using past endings. This is two pairs per word class, not three; it extends rather than replaces the earlier verb-form mama batch.

sources.publisher: The Japan Foundation, Minna no Kyozai
sources.section: Actual HTML heading まま and structure chart Nの / Aい / ANな / Vた / Vない. Explanation A describes an unchanged state and a frequent, not obligatory, negative evaluation; noun example 4 and na-adjective example 6 were inspected. Explanation B covers deliberately keeping a state, with i-adjective example 8. Explanation C and example 11 include きれいなままになっている, not a simple new-change reading of naru. Teacher notes distinguish simultaneous activity and other conformity uses. Simplified extraction returned only a helpfulness counter, so the actual HTML body/chart was inspected.

sources.publisher: The Japan Foundation, Minna no Kyozai
sources.section: Actual HTML heading Aく/ANに/Nになります, structure chart, explanations A/B, clean-room example 5 and student-year example 6. The result of a change is foregrounded; teacher notes distinguish this from the agentive suru construction and note that a result can persist after narimashita. Old JLPT labels are not used as present-day classifications.

Actual About text: unchanged state, attributive attachment and the frequent V-ta form. Its casual manma note was inspected; these questions explicitly supply the basic kana mama ending, not an unrestricted form inventory. Broad advice about leaving things undisturbed, optional ni or emphasis is not adopted as a universal rule.
Exact 学生, gakusei, current student noun sense. Not the separate archaic gakushou/gakusou entry.
Exact 空き地/空地/明き地, akichi, vacant-land noun sense, without spelling restriction. Not the Go empty-point sense. Recognition supports accepted orthography, not equal frequency.
Exact 静か/閑か, shizuka, na-adjective quiet/silent sense without spelling restriction; not the slow/unhurried sense or adjacent expressions. Model retains 静か.

Exact 綺麗/奇麗, kirei, with kana reading キレイ also listed. The clean/tidy sense is a na-adjective and marked usually written in kana. Do not classify it as an i-adjective from its last sound or substitute the adverbial completely sense.

Exact 冷たい i-adjective with tsumetai and the variant reading tsubetai; the physical-cold sense has no reading restriction. A separate lookup of つべたい returned the same entry. Corresponding kana forms are accepted without recommending tsubetai as the default pronunciation or inferring frequency from dictionary inclusion. The emotional-coldness sense is not the water task.
Exact 高い, takai, i-adjective expensive/high-priced sense. Not the height, pitch or volume senses. The increase example explicitly supplies a comparison with the earlier price.

authoringNotes: All scenarios are original. The sources establish attachment and state/change meanings, not automatic naturalness of every new sentence; retain independent linguistic review.

The visible tasks name two basic past patterns for the supplied predicate: noun no-mama-datta versus ni-natta; na-adjective na-mama-datta versus ni-natta; unchanged i-adjective mama-datta versus its ku form natta. Predicate orthography may be kana or kanji, but the supplied endings remain kana. Other copular expansions, mama-ni-natteita, manma and alternative whole-sentence paraphrases are outside this bounded task, not globally wrong.

Both question text and translation establish the relevant interval and ask for persistence or a transition. The contrast is not between any two sentences that happen to end in the same present state. A state may become true and subsequently persist; those descriptions concern different aspects or intervals.

The retained student status allows a change of year level, and the vacant lot allows cut grass. Retention concerns the named property, not every detail of an object or person's life. The clean floor remains clean during yesterday's opening hours but is dirty this morning, avoiding an inference that past mama-datta guarantees persistence to the present.

Quiet, a clean floor and deliberately chilled water balance the unwelcome continuing expense. Mama does not require carelessness or a bad outcome. The deliberate enrollment and cleaning also prevent a rule that naru changes must happen without human intention or action.

Kirei is explicitly a na-adjective despite its final i sound. Named predicates recur on both sides. Include source-recognized spellings and the cold adjective's recorded reading, explain them in feedback, and keep ordinary model forms; acceptance is not a frequency or recommendation claim.

The full linked article inventory and existing mama verb-state batch were screened. These prompts name mama/naru patterns rather than asking unrestricted selection among tokoro, nagara, negative-without, self-assessment or purpose expressions. They do not independently test every possible conformity use or all negative noun/adjective states.

An additional broad web search returned no relevant results. The existing source guide and batch records led to the actual JPF pages, which provided the required evidence without treating the failed search as a source.

All281 previous exercise records and identities remain unchanged. The article gains one scoped subsection, its existing JPF mama reference is expanded to name the chart's noun/adjective coverage, and one lexical-reference bullet is added. No prior exercise or unrelated article prose is rewritten. One exercise/SRS identity covers spelling and presentation alternatives.
